To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a modal decomposition analysis of combustor pressure time history data is possible.

a restricted modal analysis can be successfully used to decompose the pressure field in an engine combustor and the cut-on frequencies for this particular engine are close to each other at each operating condition and consequently the spectrum related to the modal content of the pressure field does not change much with engine operating condition.
the restricted modal decomposition of the combustor pressure field, as measured by two pressure time histories, is a viable method for analyzing combustor pressure spectra and cross-spectra.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an understanding of the pressure field inside a combustor.
the decomposition of a pressure signal into its constituent circumferential mode components.
the development and application of a restricted modal analysis technique to internal annular combustors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the modal span frequencies are a useful and practical tool for the analysis of combustor pressure field time history measurements.
the modal decomposition is not very useful in the analysis of combustion noise.
for this engine the combustion noise spectrum is not very dependent on operating condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the modal decomposition of a combustion chamber pressure field as determined by two time history measurements is a viable approach for combustion noise analysis, and that this restricted modal analysis approach is applicable to the PW4098 engine.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to use the restricted modal decomposition technique to analyze the combustion noise spectra of the internal annular combustor.

we have shown that the modal decomposition of pressure time history data can be successfully applied to a combustor and that this method is applicable over a wide range of operating conditions and engine types.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the restricted modal analysis can be applied successfully to the analysis of combustor autospectra and cross spectra data.
the restricted modal decomposition of the autospectra and cross-spectra of a combustor can be used to identify the presence of circumferential mode pairs at specific frequencies.
a restricted modal analysis can be used to determine the modal decomposition of a pressure field in a duct.
